News global nation business lifestyle entertainment technology sports opinion LATEST NEWS STORIES HEADLINES METRO REGIONS NATION WORLD CDN NEWSLETTER www / Philippine Elections Philippine Elections Comelec expects 4 million new registrants for 2028 By: Dianne Sampang - @inquirerdotnet INQUIRER.net / 05:00 AM November 23, 2026 Share: MANILA, Philippines — Commission on Elections chair George Erwin Garcia on Sunday predicted that four million more Filipinos will register for the May 8, 2028 national elections, which could bring the total number of registered voters to 75 million.
After resuming its registration drive on Nov. 10, the agency has received 140,000 to 150,000 applications, with Garcia observing that many of the early registrants were young Filipinos. Registration is open until July 30, 2027.
Comelec earlier said it was targeting 3 million new registrants to raise the total number of registered voters to 74 million from the current 71 million, but Garcia was optimistic the agency could raise the figure by 1 million more.
READ: Registering to vote in 2028? Here’s what you need to know
“We see that this will exceed our estimate of 3 million [new voter registrants], and we might reach around 4 million,” he said in an interview over dzBB.
“That’s good news because 2028 is a very crucial, critical, and important election in our country because we will elect our new president and vice president and other national and local positions.”
READ: Comelec logs over 170,000 voter registrations for 2028 elections
To register as a voter, an individual must be at least 18 years old on or before May 8, 2028, and residing in the Philippines for at least one year and in the place where they intend to vote for at least six months immediately preceding the elections.
Garcia also dismissed speculations about a “no-el” (no elections) scenario in 2028.
“That is impossible to happen. The 1987 Constitution says that there shall be elections in 2028. The Congress cannot make any law that will be signed by the President to change the Constitution. Therefore, we guarantee 100 percent that there will be elections in 2028,’’ he said.
Paolo Panelo, spokesperson for Vice President Sara Duterte, told Bilyonaryo News Channel that she had received information about a “no-el” plan in 2028.
House Senior Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez on Thursday debunked the claims that lawmakers were hatching plans to postpone the 2028 elections.
Garcia said the elections for president and vice president cannot be likened to the barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections (BSKE), which have been postponed by Congress a number of times.
“The terms of the president and vice president cannot be changed because we don’t have a holdover capacity. Their terms will end at noon of June 30, 2028,” he said.
